chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Hudhayni, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about completing (the prayer) and shortening (it). He said: 'When you enter the two Sanctuaries, intend ten days and complete the prayer.' I said to him: 'I arrive in Mecca one or two or three days before Tarwiyah.' He said: 'Intend staying ten days and complete the prayer.'

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: The day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.انْوِ: Intend (as in niyyah for prayer duration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening or completing prayers for a traveler entering Mecca before the Hajj days?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific application of the *iqamah* (ten-day stay) rule for travelers entering the two holy sanctuaries, Mecca and Medina. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that the intention of staying ten days is the decisive factor for performing full prayers, even if the traveler arrives days before the main Hajj rituals like Tarwiyah, thereby extending the traveler's status to that of a resident for prayer purposes.
